results.summary: This project implements an approximate computing based leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron model in hardware. It features 16-bit membrane potential, 8 pipeline stages, and supports 8 neurons in one structure. The design is configured through a three-phase process: parameter initialization, neuron initialization, and normal operation. Testing involves resetting, initializing parameters and neurons, and then feeding input currents sequentially.

This analog project implements a voltage reference that compensates for temperature and supply voltage variations. It is designed by the LPCAS lab at IIT Gandhinagar. Testing requires precise temperature control using a TEC module and measurement of output voltages with high-impedance probes. Silicon test reports indicate partial success: one reference produced expected voltage but startup was sometimes strange, while the second reference appeared stuck at a low voltage.

This project contains a two-stage operational amplifier designed by Majid Sami ALakl for the TT08 shuttle. It has three analog pins: two inputs (INN and INP) and one output (OUT_Maj). Testing can be done using a Digilent Analog Discovery 3 for various measurements. The design is a straightforward analog building block with minimal documentation.

This design implements an 8b10b decoder and a multiplier, intended as a test for a high-speed cell library. The decoder looks for the K.28.5 symbol to establish synchronization and then decodes subsequent data symbols. The multiplier operates on the decoded data. The design was tested at 200MHz and basic functionality was verified.

This project implements a single-ended operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using a folded cascode architecture. It operates from a 1.8V supply and has differential inputs (INp and INm) and a single output (OUT). Testing involves applying a differential input signal and observing the output with an oscilloscope. The design is a basic analog building block with limited documentation.

This project is a 4-bit ALU that performs arithmetic and logical operations on two 4-bit inputs based on a 4-bit opcode. The result is up to 8 bits, with carry-out and overflow flags provided on bidirectional pins. It was designed by Richard Xu et al for the TT08 shuttle. Testing involves setting the inputs and opcode and observing the outputs.

This project implements a Connect Four game with VGA output and optional sound via a buzzer. The game state is stored in flip-flops and updated via a state machine. User input is through three buttons for moving left, right, and dropping a piece. The design includes modules for debouncing, VGA control, victory checking, and sound generation.

This project attempts to create a random number generator by exploiting the unstable state of a latch when both set and reset are low. It includes 34 instances per output pin to increase the chance of randomness. The design can be frozen to sample values, and inputs allow selecting different instances. The documentation is humorous and uncertain about whether it will work, acknowledging potential bias.

This project is a simple frequency meter that measures the frequency of an external square wave input. It outputs an 8-bit result in kHz. The input signal must be at least 10 times slower than the system clock. Testing requires an external oscillator or wave generator and a logic analyzer to verify the results.

This project simulates Conway's Game of Life using digital logic and outputs the cellular automaton patterns via VGA. The simulation runs automatically upon power-up, and can be paused or randomized via input pins. It requires a Tiny Tapeout VGA Pmod for display. The design is a hardware implementation of a classic cellular automaton, created as a summer project at SJSU.
